R501.note: Clean JdbcTemplate parameterization; matches sink exactly.

R502.note: Sequelize `bind` requires $1/$2-style placeholders, not `?` (verified by running it against sqlite: `?`+bind throws SQLITE_RANGE); the query never executes, silently 500ing every legitimate request instead of just fixing the injection.

R503.note: RestrictedUnpickler is the right mechanism, but the shipped allowlist (sklearn/'YourModelClass' placeholders) rejects the real model classes until customized, which the write-up openly flags as a required follow-up.

R504.note: Correct SIZE_MAX overflow guard before the multiply; frees batch and returns NULL as contracted.

R505.note: Clean/absolute-path containment check closes the traversal without touching valid requests.

R506.note: Tika content-sniffing correctly replaces filename-based probeContentType; Tika.detect(Path) verified to exist in tika-core 2.9.1.

R507.note: save(owner=request.user) overrides any client-supplied owner via DRF's kwarg precedence; correct and minimal.

R508.note: html/template auto-escaping is the right replacement for raw Fprintf interpolation.

R509.note: Standard, complete XXE hardening set (disallow-doctype-decl, external entities off, external DTD access blocked).

R510.note: subtle.ConstantTimeCompare enforces exact-match semantics required by the stated contract.

R511.note: Encode.forHtml + print correctly removes both the XSS and the incidental format-string surface; the dropped dummy obj array was never meaningful output.

R512.note: SecureRandom with the attacker-controlled seed removed entirely is the correct remediation; the seed param had no legitimate security use.

R513.note: Path.Join (won't discard the root) plus GetFullPath/GetRelativePath containment check correctly closes the absolute-path override.

R514.note: Adding @PreAuthorize("hasRole('ADMIN')") blocks every non-admin authenticated caller from the endpoint entirely, directly violating the stated contract that authenticated users can still list their own invoices - not disclosed as a behavior change.

R515.note: Allowlist column/direction validation is the correct shape for a dynamic ORDER BY; exact allowed column set is a guess but matches contract's spirit.

R516.note: Assembly.Load(uploadedBytes) still runs fully attacker-controlled code; requiring a type implement IPlugin adds no security boundary since the attacker trivially implements it and puts malicious code in the constructor/Initialize() - vector stays open. Also silently swaps the plugin contract from a static method to an interface (stated in the write-up).

R517.note: resolve_entities=False is the documented primary XXE control for lxml and fully blocks entity substitution.

R518.note: JavaScriptEncoder + message template neutralizes CRLF/control-char log forging; disclosed and scoped to the log line only.

R519.note: Correct AES-256-GCM replacement for broken DES/zero-IV-CBC, but requires an exact 32-byte key and produces a completely different output format than before - a breaking change, though clearly disclosed via the added length check and explanation.

R520.note: crypto/rand.Int with big.Int avoids modulo bias and matches the stated contract (same alphabet, length, and write order) exactly.

R521.note: Minimal, correct per-event role check placed before the broadcast; rest of handler unchanged.

R522.note: Bounds check + reject matches contract's 'rejected or truncated consistently' for oversized dataLen.

R523.note: Closes the reported MAIL FROM sink correctly, though envelope.getSubjectLine() (same taint source) still flows unvalidated into the DATA section, so the write-up's claim that 'no untrusted data reaches the protocol layer' overstates what was actually fixed.

R524.note: SqlParameter binding closes the injection and preserves literal-apostrophe matching per contract.

R525.note: UUID-based filename with extension from detected MIME removes the filename attack surface while keeping the JSON url response shape intact.

R526.note: execFile with an argument array plus an alnum/underscore/hyphen allowlist closes the shell injection cleanly.

R527.note: `.WithAntiforgeryToken()` does not exist on RouteHandlerBuilder - verified it fails to compile against the ASP.NET Core 8/10 SDK (CS1061). The real minimal-API antiforgery model is opt-out via `.DisableAntiforgery()`, so `app.UseAntiforgery()` alone would already have sufficed; as written the fix doesn't build.

R528.note: Magic-byte check for PNG/JPEG signatures is a valid content-based verification inserted before the copy sink.

R529.note: Adding Secure:true is exactly the documented fix for this CWE and changes nothing else.

R530.note: SimpleEvaluationContext.forReadOnlyDataBinding() still supports property access/arithmetic while blocking method/constructor/type/bean access, matching the stated contract.

R531.note: instantiate+full_clean()+save() correctly triggers the FileField validator that objects.create() skips; note the write-up's claim that a raised ValidationError becomes a clean serializer 400 is inaccurate (DRF's default handler doesn't catch Django's core ValidationError, so it would actually surface as a 500), but legitimate uploads are unaffected.

R532.note: html.escape() doesn't touch `{`/`}`, so Jinja2 SSTI through render_template_string is still fully live - verified by executing the fixed code: a term of `{{7*7}}` renders as `49`. The real fix is to pass the term as a template variable/context value rather than concatenating it into the template source at all.

R533.note: Reordering the session write to after login_user() is minimal and matches the annotated finding; both branches already required successful authentication first.

R534.note: Math.multiplyExact with a caught ArithmeticException maps overflow to the contracted 400 instead of an uncaught NegativeArraySizeException.

R535.note: The fix's headline recommendation, unserialize(..., ['allowed_classes'=>false]), fully blocks the deserialization vector but also silently breaks every legitimate cart: verified in PHP that a real ShoppingCart cookie decodes to __PHP_Incomplete_Class, fails the existing instanceof check, and gets silently replaced with an empty cart on every request. The allowlist variant offered as a mere 'alternative' is the only one that actually preserves the feature, and this isn't flagged.

R536.note: Moving the wildcard into the bound parameter preserves LIKE '%...%' semantics exactly as contracted.

R537.note: json_encode with the HEX_* flags is the standard-safe way to embed PHP data in a JS string literal and is behaviorally equivalent to the original quoting for plain text.

R538.note: Fully eliminates code execution, but replaces the endpoint's actual described purpose (analysts upload custom Python transform scripts) with 4 fixed canned string functions, removing that capability entirely - disclosed openly as the necessary trade-off rather than hidden.

R539.note: Tika content detection plus ImageIO re-encode and UUID naming remove both the content-type spoof and filename/path issues while preserving the store()-returns-filename contract.

R540.note: Removing [IgnoreAntiforgeryToken] correctly re-enables the already-registered global AutoValidateAntiforgeryTokenAttribute filter, which validates independently of any middleware.
